Housing prices per m² in Haute-Garonne, 2025

Cleaning and describing DVF transactions with R

Author

Benjamin Green

Published

October 26, 2026

Question and main results

What was the price per m² of houses and flats sold in Haute-Garonne in 2025, and how does it differ by dwelling type, location and month?

  • The sample is 19,230 sales out of 28,016 recorded transactions (69%), each containing exactly one house or flat.
  • The median price is 2,951 EUR/m² for flats and 2,695 EUR/m² for houses.
  • That gap comes from where each type is sold, not from a flat premium: 65% of flats but only 13% of houses are in Toulouse. Within Toulouse houses are more expensive (3,692 vs 3,250); outside Toulouse the two types are almost the same (2,597 vs 2,619).
  • Monthly median prices are flat through the year; sales volumes are not.
  • The results move by less than 1% when any cleaning threshold is changed.

Data

Source: DVF géolocalisées (Etalab), derived from the DGFiP Demandes de valeurs foncières, national file for 2025, filtered to département 31. One row of the raw file is a parcel or a premises, not a sale: the price of the whole sale is repeated on every row. The unit of analysis is therefore the sale (id_mutation), and the cleaning works at that level.

Cleaning

A sale is kept if it is an ordinary sale (Vente) of exactly one house or flat, with no professional premises in the same deed, a known price, and a plausible price, surface and price per m². Each step removes sales, and the table shows how many.

Step Sales left Removed
All sales in departement 31 28,016 NA
Nature = Vente 26,168 1,848
At least one house or flat 20,235 5,933
Exactly one dwelling 19,568 667
No professional premises 19,378 190
Price not missing 19,358 20
Price >= 10000 EUR 19,318 40
Surface in (0, 400] m2 19,313 5
Price/m2 in [300, 10000] 19,230 83

The thresholds are prix_min = 10,000 EUR, surface_max = 400 m², and price per m² between 300 and 10,000 EUR. They come from orders of magnitude of the market, not from the data, which is why the robustness section below varies them.

Results

By dwelling type

Type Sales Q1 Median Q3 Median surface (m²)
Appartement 10,407 2,401 2,951 3,690 55
Maison 8,823 2,072 2,695 3,292 100

Medians and quartiles are used instead of means because the distribution of price per m² is right-skewed.

Toulouse against the rest of the département

Zone Type Sales Median EUR/m² Median surface (m²)
Rest of the 31 Appartement 3,612 2,619 55
Rest of the 31 Maison 7,656 2,597 100
Toulouse Appartement 6,795 3,250 55
Toulouse Maison 1,167 3,692 95

This is a descriptive comparison, not an adjusted one: location, size and condition are not controlled for. Houses also include the land, which flats do not, so the two types are not like-for-like.

By commune

Among communes with at least 30 sales, medians run from about 1,064 EUR/m² (Montrejeau, 49 sales) to about 3,560 (Quint, 64 sales).

By month

Monthly medians stay between 2,759 and 2,900 EUR/m². The number of sales ranges from 1,238 to 2,153, with the peak in July. Toulouse’s share of monthly sales stays within a narrow band, so the mix between zones does not explain the monthly pattern.

December is the second busiest month in the final sample, 21% above the January–November average. In the full file the December excess is larger, and part of it comes from new-build sales (VEFA), which are 12.9% of December transactions against 4.7% in the other months and are excluded by the cleaning. The excess does not disappear after the cleaning, and I have not established why: this analysis does not test any explanation.

Robustness

Each threshold is changed on its own, the other three staying at their baseline value. The largest change in a median, for any type, is 0.97%, and for the whole sample 0.53%.

prix_min 5,000 19,231 1 0.00
prix_min 20,000 19,211 -19 0.04
prix_min 30,000 19,175 -55 0.10

prix_m2_min 800 18,939 -291 0.53
prix_m2_max 8,000 19,181 -49 -0.08
prix_m2_max 15,000 19,254 24 0.05

The price-per-m² bounds remove 83 sales: 48 below the floor and 35 above the ceiling.

Side Type Sales Median price (EUR) Median surface (m²) Median EUR/m²
au-dessus du plafond Appartement 14 251,825 20.0 11,505.5556
au-dessus du plafond Maison 21 1,200,000 86.0 14,857.1429
sous le plancher Appartement 10 15,000 76.5 228.2986
sous le plancher Maison 38 24,785 120.0 219.2158

Sales under the floor have a median price of roughly 15,000 to 25,000 EUR, which is not a plausible price for a whole dwelling; they may be partial interests or entry errors. The high side mixes very small surfaces with high prices and a few expensive houses. I did not check these sales one by one.

Limits

  • One year of data, and a description only: no causal claim is made.
  • Sales with several dwellings or with professional premises are excluded, so the sample covers simple residential sales and not the whole market.
  • The price per m² is the price of the whole sale divided by the built surface. Condition, floor, outbuildings and land are not observed.
  • Two identical flats on the same parcel in one sale would count as one dwelling and double the price per m²; the upper bound limits the effect.
  • Communes with few sales have unreliable medians, hence the minimum of 30 sales for the commune comparison.

Reproducing this report

The raw file is not in the repository. Place full-2025.csv.gz in data/raw/, then run R/02_filter_31.R, R/03_clean.R, R/04_describe.R and R/05_robustness.R in this order, and render report/dvf_report.qmd.
